org_name: VeTouch: Pet Vaccine & Care Clinic
site_updates:
One Sunday per month (usually the first Sunday): 9am-1pm. We are an appointment-only clinic. Due to extremely high demand, VeTouch books appointments 2 months out. Our appointment request form (available over email: vetouch@umn.edu) opens the morning after our monthly clinic. When we are at capacity we do not accept any new appointment requests. 

Address: 2501 Minnehaha Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55404 (Chuck & Don’s Pet Wellness Center)
Parking: Street parking
Time: 9am-1pm
Dates: Clinics are typically the first Sunday of every month. Upcoming dates: May 5, 2024 (fully booked), June 2, 2024 (form opens May 6th at 8 am), and July 14, 2024 

Check-in will be at back of building

At Ve-TOUCH Clinics, University of Minnesota veterinary students provide free vaccines and preventatives for dogs and cats. We provide physical exams, rabies and distemper vaccines, and flea/tick/heartworm preventatives for no cost. WE DO NOT PROVIDE SPAYS/NEUTERS.

Since we only have 1 clinic per month and are not a full-service veterinary clinic, we are unable to see sick pets or pets with serious veterinary conditions.

- Maximum of 2 pets per owner at one clinic.
- Pets must be on a leash or in a carrier. 
- Animals older than 1 year must be spayed or neutered after their first visit to VeTouch to be seen a second time.
- We will not accommodate pets that are used for breeding, and will not accommodate their litters of puppies/kittens 

To qualify for VeTouch services, clients need to be receiving some form of public assistance. Options for qualification include: 
- Food Stamps 
- Currently unhoused
- Free or Reduced Lunch Program
- HUD Section 8 Housing
- Major V. A. Disability
- Medicaid
- Medical Assistance
- Minnesota Care
- SSD
- SSI
- Temporary Assistance for Needy Families
- WIC
- A family of four making under $40,000 per year

Email: vetouch@umn.edu
Phone: ‪(612) 440-6147 (phone messages are checked weekly on Saturdays)
Website: https://vetouch.umn.edu/

site_updates:
Speakeasy MPLS is a mutual aid side base in Uptown Minneapolis. We are a highly curated, eco-friendly thrift/general "store" that runs on donations. We provide beautiful, high-quality items that are accessible to everyone.

How it works:
1. Come in during open hours (Fri-Sat, noon-5) or schedule in-person browsing through our linktr.ee if you need a personalized experience (for the immunocompromised, those with sensory/accessibility needs, etc.). DM with any questions.

2. TO CLAIM AN ITEM: DM to confirm availability. Most items can be held through the weekend. Furniture requires a $20 Venmo donation to hold, and pick-up must be scheduled through our linktr.ee. 

3. Reparations model: everything is free for BIPOC - tell us what you need or want for yourself or others (whether it's been posted or not) and if we have it, it's yours. Colonizers (white folks), Donate What You Can as an act of voluntary reparations via Venmo (@SpeakeasyMpls) - if your budget is the Dollar Store, treat us like the Dollar Store; if your budget is Anthropologie, donate like you're shopping at Anthropologie (or anything in between) - and if you're unable to donate at all, we understand.

org_name: VEAP (Volunteers Enlisted to Assist People)
site_updates:
Your first step, whether you need food, resources for your children, or simply to speak with our Social Services team is to call us at 952-888-9616. Volunteers will gather information and explain VEAP’s programs. Our call intake center is open Monday – Friday from 9:00 a.m. – 4:30 p.m.

Drop-offs 
M-F 9:00am-4:30pm, no appointment needed; pull around to door 4.

Serves residents of Edina, Richfield, Bloomington, and Minneapolis south of 50th St./west of Cedar. You will need a photo ID and a piece of mail (like a utility bill) that shows your address. 

VEAP’s On-site Food Pantry offers a visitor-choice model; you visit the pantry, you are able to select the food you know your family will use and enjoy. Receive up to 18 household visits per year, including 12 monthly full pantry visits and 6 supplemental produce visits (produce plus 10 items from the non-perishable, meats, dairy and eggs section). 

VEAP offers a variety of fresh foods, including fruits and vegetables, an assortment of meats, and dairy, as well as basic food staples, like rice, beans, cereals, and canned products, daily.

Also is a partner of People & Pets Together that helps families facing economic hardship by providing pet food to food shelves in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan area

If you are new to VEAP, you have the opportunity to meet with a member of VEAP’s Social Services team to learn more about other supportive services that are available to you and your family. If you will need a ride home with your groceries, please let us know when you make your appointment. Delivery is also available five days a week to folks with limited mobility.

https://veap.org/get-help/veap-programs/food/

At Big Lake Community Food Shelf, we treat our clients with the utmost dignity and respect they deserve. We are located in city hall.

We are a choice model food shelf, which means you will select the food you want. Due to Covid-19, we are currently using a paper (Thursday) or on-line (Monday/Wednesday) choice list, and volunteers pack your food for you.
- Mondays and Wednesdays are on-line ordering by appointment only.  Appointments must be set up 24 hours prior to service time.
- Thursdays are for walk-ins – no appointment needed.
- Tuesday and Friday events are extra events that do not affect your regular monthly visit.

Throughout the year, we offer special meals to help families get through traditionally hard seasons. Special services include Summer Kids Kits, Holiday Meal Bags, Birthday Bags, and Free Produce Days.
Learn more at https://blcfs.org/get-help/

DONATIONS

org_name: Friends in Need Food Shelf
site_updates:
Open (by appointment) Tuesdays 8am-4pm and Wednesdays 5:30pm-6:30pm.

Our main service area is Cottage Grove, Newport, St. Paul Park, and Grey Cloud Island, but we will help anyone in need of food, regardless of where they live. (Deliveries and our non-food programs are only for those in our service area.) We are pleased to offer fresh produce, deli, dairy, meat, milk, eggs, non-perishables, toiletries, and pet food in a grocery store-style setting. We allow clients to come every other week and we give out a very generous amount of food on each visit. We request that every time you visit the Friends in Need Food Shelf you bring picture identification and a current bill showing your address in our service area.  The bill can be a rent statement or receipt, utility bill, phone bill or any other bill dated recently.  If you are homeless, mention this when you call.

To make an appointment, call (651) 458-0730 on Mondays between 12:00-3:00, or Tuesdays between 7:30am-4:00pm to make an appointment. 
If you are disabled or lack transportation and would like to request delivery, call between 12pm and 3pm on Monday to set up a Tuesday delivery appointment. If you would like curbside pickup instead of coming inside to shop, please call between 12pm and 3pm on Monday to make a special appointment. When you arrive, park in our specially marked "Curbside" parking spot and call (651) 458-0730, and we'll bring food out to the car.

If none of these days or times work for you, we will be happy to make special accommodations. Please call (651) 458-0730. For a video tour of the food shelf, and info about other resources, see our website: https://www.finfood.org/get-help.html

site_updates:
Food Shelf
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. & 2:00 – 4:00 p.m.
Wednesday: closed in the morning, 4:00 – 7:00 p.m.

Donations accepted:
Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 8:30am - 4pm
Wednesday: 8:30am - 6pm

The center is between the Wendy’s and Arby’s on the corner of Fairview and University. No appointment or advanced registration is required. Food shelf participants are served on a first come, first served basis

https://keystoneservices.org/food-shelf/ 
Please call 651-917-3792 if you have any questions.

Delivery Program
Keystone launched a free delivery program to help more low-income seniors and adults with disabilities access food support. Those who qualify can receive monthly deliveries, dropped off by Keystone volunteers. Learn more about this program and if you qualify: https://keystoneservices.org/seniors/grocery-delivery/
